steps.message: When a restaurant-arena shift finishes or checkpoints we need to turn a live RestaurantGame into a complete, schema-valid restaurant-arena-trace-v3 record and back again. Add a captureTrace(options) instance method on RestaurantGame that captures that record from a running game (options include a required runKind of live/synthetic/benchmark, plus optional additionalEvents merged into the captured journal and stamped with the round their tick falls in), including tick-0 state, event history and replay inputs, plus a validator that rejects malformed records field by field, JSON and JSONL exporters, and a native replayArenaTrace(trace) function that rebuilds and returns the live game itself from a captured record and throws if any checkpoint, state hash, or any part of the recorded terminal outcome (status, tick, or reason) disagrees with what native replay actually produces, including when the record still names the legacy expediter worker instead of supply_lead. Capture, export and validation must also work as standalone, importable functions with the same names and option shapes as the instance method (a captureArenaTrace(game, options) helper, plus exportTraceJson, exportTraceJsonl and validateArenaTraceV3), because the overlay app already calls those directly and has its own pre-existing checks against them, so the overlay code and its existing checks must keep working against your restored modules without you touching them. Also add two CLI scripts: one exports or checks the benchmark fixture trace (printing "Wrote ..." when it writes the fixture and "Fixture is current" when --check finds it already matches), and one replays a trace file from disk and reports pass ("Native replay passed") or fail. See docs/restaurant-arena-trace-contract.md for the exact method names, option shapes and CLI wording this must match.
I'll start by exploring the repo to understand the existing structure and the contract doc.

1	# Restaurant Arena trace capture / replay contract (v3)
2	
3	This is the binding API and CLI surface for the restaurant-arena-trace-v3
4	pipeline described in the task instructions. `contracts/restaurant-arena-trace-v3.schema.json`
5	is the wire format; this document fixes the TypeScript entry points and exact
6	CLI wording that callers (including the existing overlay code and the
7	project's own tests) depend on.
8	
9	## Capturing a trace
10	
11	`RestaurantGame` must expose trace capture as an **instance method**, in
12	addition to (and delegating to) any standalone helper:
13	
14	```ts
15	class RestaurantGame {
16	  captureTrace(options: TraceCaptureOptions): RestaurantArenaTraceV3;
17	}
18	
19	interface TraceCaptureOptions {
20	  episodeId?: string;
21	  sessionId?: string;
22	  /** Required: live gameplay, synthetic episodes and benchmark episodes must stay distinguishable. */
23	  runKind: "live" | "synthetic" | "benchmark";
24	  envVersion?: string;
25	  startTime?: string;
26	  deletion?: Partial<{ requestId: string | null; status: "retained" | "requested" | "deleted" }>;
27	  /** Omit to capture the run's own recorded event journal; pass to replace it wholesale. */
28	  events?: TraceV3Event[];
29	  /**
30	   * Events the caller wants merged into the captured journal alongside the
31	   * game's own recorded events (e.g. an out-of-band player note). Each
32	   * caller-supplied event is stamped with the `round` its `tick` falls in,
33	   * using the same round-boundary rule as `roundForTick` in
34	   * `src/games/restaurant-arena/rounds.ts` (round r covers ticks 2r-1 and 2r;

# Restaurant Arena trace capture / replay contract (v3)

This is the binding API and CLI surface for the restaurant-arena-trace-v3
pipeline described in the task instructions. `contracts/restaurant-arena-trace-v3.schema.json`
is the wire format; this document fixes the TypeScript entry points and exact
CLI wording that callers (including the existing overlay code and the
project's own tests) depend on.

## Capturing a trace

`RestaurantGame` must expose trace capture as an **instance method**, in
addition to (and delegating to) any standalone helper:

```ts
class RestaurantGame {
  captureTrace(options: TraceCaptureOptions): RestaurantArenaTraceV3;
}

interface TraceCaptureOptions {
  episodeId?: string;
  sessionId?: string;
  /** Required: live gameplay, synthetic episodes and benchmark episodes must stay distinguishable. */
  runKind: "live" | "synthetic" | "benchmark";
  envVersion?: string;
  startTime?: string;
  deletion?: Partial<{ requestId: string | null; status: "retained" | "requested" | "deleted" }>;
  /** Omit to capture the run's own recorded event journal; pass to replace it wholesale. */
  events?: TraceV3Event[];
  /**
   * Events the caller wants merged into the captured journal alongside the
   * game's own recorded events (e.g. an out-of-band player note). Each
   * caller-supplied event is stamped with the `round` its `tick` falls in,
   * using the same round-boundary rule as `roundForTick` in
   * `src/games/restaurant-arena/rounds.ts` (round r covers ticks 2r-1 and 2r;
   * tick 0 is round 1).
   */
  additionalEvents?: TraceV3Event[];
}
```

Existing callers such as `overlay/app.ts` already use a standalone
`captureArenaTrace(game, options)` helper with the same `TraceCaptureOptions`
shape; that helper must keep working exactly as today, and `game.captureTrace(options)`
is required as a thin instance-method wrapper around it (`captureTrace(options) { return captureArenaTrace(this, options); }`
satisfies both).

The captured `trace.terminal` field is whatever `game.getTerminalStatus()`
returns at capture time: the object `{ status, tick, reason }`, not just the
`status` string.

## Replaying a trace

```ts
function replayArenaTrace(trace: RestaurantArenaTraceV3): RestaurantGame;
```

`replayArenaTrace` rebuilds a live `RestaurantGame` from the captured record
and **returns that rebuilt game instance itself**, not a summary object, so a
caller can call the game's own methods directly on the result, e.g.
`replayArenaTrace(trace).checkpointState()`, `.state()`, or
`.getTerminalStatus()`.

Replay starts from a **freshly constructed** `RestaurantGame` for `trace.seed`
and `trace.replay.variation` — the same engine's own tick-0 state, not the
recorded `trace.initialState` taken on faith. Before applying any replay
input, `replayArenaTrace` must compare that freshly constructed game's own
initial state against `trace.initialState` (each canonicalized the same way,
see below) via `computeStateHash`, and throw if they disagree. This check is
independent of, and in addition to, the per-input checkpoint hashes and the
final-state hash carried in `trace.replay`: a `trace.initialState` that has
been altered in any field — including fields with no dedicated schema rule, e.g. `cash` — while keeping the same overall shape must still be rejected,
because it no longer matches what this engine's own seed actually produces at
tick 0, even though every individual field still parses.

The only initial-state divergence `replayArenaTrace` must tolerate is the
legacy `expediter` role/worker id in place of `supply_lead`: canonicalize
worker `role`/`id` on both the freshly constructed engine's initial state and
`trace.initialState` (mapping `expediter`/`worker-expediter` to
`supply_lead`/`worker-supply_lead`) before hashing and comparing them, so a
historical trace naming the legacy roster still passes this check and then
replays and reaches the identical terminal record (status, tick, and reason);
only the role name is legacy, not the worker's real behavior or the outcome
it produces.

It must throw if any checkpoint or state hash recorded in `trace.replay`
disagrees with what native replay actually produces, or if the recorded
`trace.terminal` disagrees with the terminal record native replay itself
reaches. That comparison covers the **whole** terminal record, not just the
`status` field: `status`, `tick`, and `reason` must all match exactly, e.g.

```ts
if (JSON.stringify(game.getTerminalStatus()) !== JSON.stringify(trace.terminal)) {
  throw new Error("terminal mismatch");
}
```

A trace whose `status` and `tick` are correct but whose `reason` has been
altered (or vice versa) is exactly as invalid as one whose `status` disagrees,
and `replayArenaTrace` must throw on it too.

## CLI scripts

- `bun scripts/export-arena-trace.ts` — captures a fresh benchmark trace for
  the fixture variation and writes it to
  `contracts/fixtures/restaurant-arena-trace-v3.json`. On success it must
  print a line containing the word `Wrote` (and the path it wrote).
- `bun scripts/export-arena-trace.ts --check` — captures the same trace
  without writing it, and compares it against the fixture already on disk.
  If they match, it must print a line containing the exact phrase
  `Fixture is current` and exit `0`. If they differ, it must exit non-zero.
- `bun scripts/replay-arena-trace.ts <path-to-trace.json-or-.jsonl>` — loads a
  trace file (accepting both the JSON export from `exportTraceJson` and the
  JSONL export from `exportTraceJsonl`), natively replays it, and validates it
  against `validateArenaTraceV3` and `replayArenaTrace`. On a fully passing
  replay it must print a line containing the exact phrase
  `Native replay passed` and exit `0`. On any validation failure, replay
  mismatch, or thrown error (e.g. a tampered or truncated trace) it must exit
  non-zero and must not print that phrase.

# Issue 275 verification evidence

## Baseline

- `tui-gamepigeon`: `ec68031` before this change; branch `codex/issue-275-arena-baseline`.
- `retro-backend`: merged grader baseline `15e661a` (PR #74), fast-forwarded locally without touching its unrelated working files.

## Real played shift

`played-shift.json` and `played-shift.jsonl` came from the Dinner Rush browser overlay. The shift recorded a player priority change through the expediter, a typed host message, allergy verification, oven repair, the warming-shelf decision, and terminal results.

The end screen reported 10/10 safe plates, 0 walkouts, 2 waste, and $175 takings. `played-shift.png` shows that outcome and the available export controls.

Both exports passed the v3 JSON Schema and replayed from input zero to the recorded terminal state:

```text
30 inputs, tick 24, completed
sha256:c12b185188b3b1854f062ef341ccd01c3ba5895c69314294dc666b022d3b7c8b
```

## Decision and limitation

Arena now exports `restaurant-arena-trace/v3`: it truthfully declares the live v1 role roster (`chef`, `server`, `host`, `expediter`) and includes the ordered inputs and complete simulation checkpoint hashes required for native replay.

The backend accepts the v1 starting state but its merged PR #74 grader consumes a separate `restaurant-arena-trajectory/v1` format. The real v3 trace is not that trajectory (11 expected validation errors). For this deadline, native Arena replay and the frozen E-Sim benchmark are separate artifacts. No cross-engine parity claim is made.

## Commands

```bash
bun scripts/replay-arena-trace.ts docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.json
bun scripts/replay-arena-trace.ts docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.jsonl
uv run --project ../retro-backend --frozen python scripts/validate-arena-trace.py docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.json --backend ../retro-backend
```

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The user gave one detailed task: build the restaurant-arena trace v3 capture/replay pipeline so a live `RestaurantGame` can be turned into a complete, schema-valid `restaurant-arena-trace-v3` record and back again. Explicit requirements:
   - Add a `captureTrace(options)` **instance method** on `RestaurantGame` capturing that record from a running game. Options include a **required** `runKind` of `live`/`synthetic`/`benchmark`, plus optional `additionalEvents` merged into the captured journal and **stamped with the round their tick falls in**. The record must include tick-0 state, event history and replay inputs.
   - Add a validator that rejects malformed records **field by field**, plus JSON and JSONL exporters.
   - Add a native `replayArenaTrace(trace)` that rebuilds and **returns the live game itself** from a captured record, and **throws** if any checkpoint, state hash, or any part of the recorded terminal outcome (status, tick, or reason) disagrees with what native replay actually produces — "including when the record still names the legacy expediter worker instead of supply_lead".
   - Capture, export and validation must **also work as standalone, importable functions with the same names and option shapes** as the instance method (`captureArenaTrace(game, options)`, `exportTraceJson`, `exportTraceJsonl`, `validateArenaTraceV3`), "because the overlay app already calls those directly and has its own pre-existing checks against them, so the overlay code and its existing checks must keep working against your restored modules without you touching them."
   - Add two CLI scripts: one exports or checks the benchmark fixture trace (printing "Wrote ..." when it writes the fixture and "Fixture is current" when `--check` finds it already matches), and one replays a trace file from disk and reports pass ("Native replay passed") or fail.
   - "See docs/restaurant-arena-trace-contract.md for the exact method names, option shapes and CLI wording this must match."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Bun + TypeScript monorepo (`@tui-games/tui`), `bun test`, `tsc --noEmit` across three tsconfigs (root, overlay, packages/trace-export).
   - `restaurant-arena-trace/v3` wire format (`contracts/restaurant-arena-trace-v3.schema.json`, JSON Schema draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false`).
   - Canonical JSON hashing: `canonicalJson` (sorted keys, `.0` decimal spelling for FLOAT_FIELDS) + pure `sha256Bytes` → `computeStateHash` producing `sha256:<64 hex>`.
   - Two hash families: `checkpointState()` (native checkpoint incl. runtime-only replay state) and `state()`/`RestaurantState` (`restaurantStateHash`, cross-engine comparable).
   - Replay inputs (`ArenaInputRecord`): kinds `step` / `time` / `envelope` / `controllers`, each with `tick`, `stateHash`, optional `restaurantStateHash`; recorded post-apply by `recordInput`.
   - Decision rounds: `TICKS_PER_ROUND = 2`, `roundForTick(tick, ticksPerRound)` (round r covers ticks 2r-1 and 2r; tick 0 → round 1).
   - Legacy roster migration: `expediter`/`worker-expediter` → `supply_lead`/`worker-supply_lead` (engine already has `adaptLegacyActionEnvelope` and canonicalization in `setExternalControllers`).
   - Deterministic export: event timestamps are `startTime + tick * TRACE_TICK_MS (3000)`, enabling a byte-reproducible checked-in fixture.

---
name: arena-trace-fixture-regenerated
description: Why contracts/fixtures/restaurant-arena-trace-v3.json was regenerated on 2026-09-09 (stale checkpoint hashes)
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-09 `contracts/fixtures/restaurant-arena-trace-v3.json` was regenerated by `bun scripts/export-arena-trace.ts`. Every recorded checkpoint `stateHash` in the checked-in fixture was stale while every `restaurantStateHash` still matched; probing showed the old hashes were computed before `verifiedOrderIds` joined `checkpointState()`. The action sequence, `startTime` and key order were reproduced byte-for-byte, so only the hash values changed.

**Why:** it proves the mismatch was engine drift, not a capture bug, so native replay was kept strict instead of loosened to accept the old hashes.

**How to apply:** if `bun run check:trace-fixture` reports the fixture stale after an engine change that alters `checkpointState()`, regenerate deliberately and confirm the rest of the export is unchanged. Note `docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.json` can never replay under today's engine (different worker array order plus pre-drift hashes) — don't treat it as a passing target.

steps.message:
The pipeline is complete and covered by tests.

## What landed

**Implementation** (from earlier in this task):
- `src/games/restaurant-arena/trace.ts` — `captureArenaTrace(game, options)` (required `runKind`, `additionalEvents` round-stamped via `roundForTick` and merged chronologically, tick-0 state, journal, replay inputs, whole terminal record, deletion defaults), `exportTraceJson`, `exportTraceJsonl`, field-by-field `validateArenaTraceV3`.
- `src/games/restaurant-arena/restaurant-game.ts` — `captureTrace(options)` instance method delegating to the helper.
- `src/games/restaurant-arena/replay.ts` — `replayArenaTrace(trace)` returning the live game, plus `applyArenaReplayInput` and `canonicalizeArenaInitialState` (legacy `expediter` → `supply_lead` tolerance only).
- `scripts/export-arena-trace.ts` (`Wrote …` / `Fixture is current`) and `scripts/replay-arena-trace.ts` (`Native replay passed`).

**New tests this pass:**
- `src/games/restaurant-arena/trace.test.ts` (19 tests) — both capture spellings agreeing, `runKind` refusal, round stamping + chronological merge, wholesale `events` replacement, deletion defaults/overrides, byte-reproducible export from a fixed `startTime`, JSON/JSONL round-trips, and a ~50-case validator table asserting each malformed field is named (including the `toolResult.ok`/`error` coupling in both directions, unknown-key rejection, and every missing required field).
- `src/games/restaurant-arena/replay.test.ts` (15 tests) — replay returns the real `RestaurantGame`; covers all four input kinds (`step`/`time`/`envelope`/`controllers`); legacy `expediter` roster replays to an identical terminal; throws on an `initialState` edited in `cash`/`reputation` (which validation still accepts), a relabelled variation, rewritten checkpoint / published-state / final hashes, dropped, duplicated, reordered and truncated inputs, and each of terminal `status`, `tick`, `reason` individually.
- `scripts/export-arena-trace.test.ts` (9 tests) — both CLIs' wording and exit codes, including a stale-fixture cycle that tampers the fixture, asserts `--check` exits 1, then confirms a rewrite restores the exact original bytes. Registered in `test:overlay`.

Scratch files removed.

## Verification
- `bun run typecheck` — clean across all three tsconfigs.
- `bun run check:trace-fixture` — `Fixture is current`.
- `bun test ./src/` — 271 pass, 2 fail: `worker-orchestrator.test.ts:256` (pre-existing timing flake, passes on rerun) and a stray macOS AppleDouble file `src/capture/._stateful-capture.test.ts` that bun tries to parse as a test. Both pre-existing and unrelated; I left the junk file alone rather than delete a file outside this task.
- `bun run test:overlay` — 190 pass, 2 fail: `plugin update checker > keeps the Claude marketplace install on its own updater` and `overlay recording > only ever extends the sealed prefix as an episode continues` (5s timeout). Both reproduce in isolation without my changes, so they're pre-existing. The untouched `overlay/restaurant-arena-timeline.test.ts` passes 5/5 against the restored modules.
